title: Queen against Rook
subtitle: Separate the rook from the king

source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter II, §16 Queen against Rook, Examples 40–41

steps.title: A standard position
steps.source: If it were Black's move it would be simple, as he would have to move his Rook away from the King, and then the Rook would be comparatively easy to win. […] We must bring about the position in the diagram with Black to move.

narration.say: One of the most difficult endings without pawns. This is a standard defensive position.
If it were Black to move, the rook would have to leave the king, and would soon be lost.
So the plan: reach this same position, with Black to move. Your move.

feedback.Qa6: The trap every beginner falls into: Rc7 check, Kb6, Rc6 check, and Kxc6 is stalemate.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Start with a check.
exercise.success: 1. Qe5, check. Black goes to a7.

narration.say: Queen to a1, check. Black returns to b8.

feedback.*: Put the queen back where it was at the start.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Return to the starting position.
exercise.wrong: Put the queen back where it was at the start.
exercise.success: 3. Qa5. The same position, with Black to move. The rook must leave. It can only go to a light square, or a check wins it.

narration.say: Queen to e5, check. Black goes to a8, best.
Queen to h8, check; and g7, check.
Queen to g8, check. The rook must block on b8.

feedback.*: The rook has left the b3 square. Use the diagonal.

exercise.prompt: White to move and give checkmate in one.
exercise.wrong: The rook has left the b3 square. Use the diagonal.
exercise.success: Checkmate. The long-range diagonal checks did the work.

steps.title: A similar position
steps.source: The procedure here is very similar. The things to bear in mind are that the Rook must be prevented from interposing at Kt 1 because of an immediate mate, and in the same way the King must be prevented from going either to R 3 or B 1.

narration.say: Here the procedure is very similar.
Keep the rook from blocking on b8, because of an immediate mate.
And keep the black king away from a6 and c8.
Try it yourself on a board.
